entities.summary: Vettius Aquilinus (b. 250 CE) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, active in the Roman Empire. He served as a military leader and commander, playing a significant role in the empire's expansion and defense. Aquilinus's tenure spanned a period of great change and upheaval, marked by the rise of new social and economic forces. His legacy can be seen in the continued importance of the Roman administrative system in modern times. Despite the passage of centuries, Aquilinus's name remains a testament to the enduring legacy of the Roman Empire. The Roman historian Tacitus wrote of Aquilinus's military campaigns in his Histories, providing valuable insights into the life and times of this influential figure.
